claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch despite a known under-target gap in the health-plan benefits support segment because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, the affected segment is only 3% of projected first-month traffic, and post-launch documentation and monitoring can manage the residual risk.
specific_concerns: The available record says the affected segment is named in a regulated-customer pilot order form, which fits the policy's materiality trigger for contractual customer segments or named launch use cases.
The record says legal review on disclosure is still open; the policy text says low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality when legal review is pending.
The record says the segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points, and no admissible evidence provided here shows the gap was resolved before launch.
No admissible evidence provided here shows the limitation was disclosed before launch or covered by an approved risk acceptance, which the cited policy makes necessary for a material limitation.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general readiness, but they do not answer the specific materiality and disclosure predicate governing this gap.
Public governance guidance about model cards, monitoring, and measurement is not a substitute for satisfying the release policy's specific disclosure or approval requirement.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record.
That the 3% projected traffic share is sufficient to treat the weakness as non-material despite the named regulated-customer commitment and pending legal review.
That documentation and post-launch monitoring alone cure the pre-launch policy requirement.
Any implication that public model-card or risk-management guidance independently authorizes launch under the internal policy.
evidence_requests: Provide the final legal determination on whether this gap required disclosure before launch.
Provide the approved risk-acceptance record, if one exists, that specifically covers this named segment gap before launch.
Provide the actual disclosure text or customer-facing launch documentation showing the limitation was disclosed for the named use case before certification.
Provide the underlying contractual or order-form language showing whether the health-plan benefits support segment is in scope for launch commitments.
Provide the source record for the 1.5 percentage point miss and whether remediation closed it before certification.
decision_criteria: Use the policy text as the controlling standard: a weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Treat low-volume or non-core framing as insufficient when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or legal review is pending.
Require admissible evidence of one of the policy-safe conditions before certification: the issue was resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Do not let aggregate readiness metrics or generic governance guidance override a specific unresolved materiality predicate.
Assess only the evidence available to this role; do not infer missing approvals, disclosures, or legal conclusions.
